articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and president
articles.summary: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board on Monday announced that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president of the chip giant. Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news. In a statement, the board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said. Jensen Huang, Ceo di Nvidia, interviene a un evento in occasione del forum Computex, a Taipei, Taiwan, il 2 giugno 2024. REUTERS/Ann Wang Reuters / REUTERS "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's CFO." Jones will remain the chair of Nvidia's board. "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. articles.title: Iran vows to end U.S. naval blockade by 'all available means'
articles.summary: What to know about the Iran war today: Iran said Monday it would use "all available means" to counter the U.S. naval blockade of the country's ports, which a foreign ministry official described as "an act of military aggression" against the country.President Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that Iran had "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time" during the nearly-nine-month war , but that the increasing attacks had "done no damage."  A media outlet linked to Iran's Houthi allies said Monday that a Saudi attack on Yemen's port city of Hodeida killed four people and wounded 18, as fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis continues to intensify. Qatar's prime minister returns to Washington for Rubio meeting U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, in Washington, D.C., on Monday. It was the Qatari official's second visit to Washington in recent weeks, after meeting with President Trump earlier this month. At the time, Mr. Trump had said he didn't see a reason to escalate the Iran war after the midterm elections. Qatar has been a key mediator in indirect talks between the U.S. and Iran to end the conflict, which have stalled. U.S. issues dozens of new sanctions against Iran The U.S. Treasury Department issued new sanctions against a group of Iranian nationals and entities, which it described as front companies and exchange houses, on Monday. A list of two dozen names posted to its website included nine Iranian individuals in addition to businesses based, mainly, in Tehran and Dubai. The Treasury said in a news release that the sanctions came as part of "a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran's global shadow banking networks," which, according to the agency, allow billions to circulate internationally and "provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions." "Iran's economy is underwater, and its leaders are panicking," said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in a statement. "Iran's shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime. Treasury will continue dismantling these illicit networks until we have buried the head of the snake." Coalition fighting Houthis carried out hundreds of strikes in last few hours, Yemen says The military coalition fighting Houthi rebels in Yemen carried out 647 strikes in the last few hours, the Yemeni government said Monday. The attacks included drone, rocket, field artillery and airstrikes, a government spokesperson said in a social media statement . According to the spokesperson, those strikes "targeted militia positions, gatherings, fortifications and movements" and resulted in the "neutralization" of 122 Houthi commanders and members. More than 50 vehicles and pieces of military equipment were destroyed or disabled, the statement said. In a separate statement, also shared to social media , Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said the Saudi Air Force had carried out 67 airstrikes and missile attacks in the last 24 hours, and that dozens of civilians were killed or wounded. Saree said the strikes killed and wounded dozens of civilians in targeted areas of Yemen's capital, Sana'a, as well as the governorates of Lahj, Taiz, Hodeidah, Saada and Hajjah. But the Yemeni government blamed the Houthis for a missile attack Monday in Taiz, where, its spokesperson said, two civilians were killed and seven others were injured in the village of Kahlan. Houthis say death toll from Saudi attack has risen to 17 Yemen's Houthi rebels said the death toll from a Saudi attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida rose to 17 Monday. The Iran-backed fighters, who control a massive portion of Yemen, including Hodeida, are battling a Saudi-led coalition that supports Yemen's internationally recognized government. Coalition airstrikes on telecommunication facilities killed 17 workers, wounded 11 more and caused the "total destruction" of administrative buildings, staff housing, a mosque and other infrastructure on the compound, the Houthis' telecommunications ministry said. "This has led to the complete destruction of these facilities [and] the disruption of telecommunications and internet services," affecting tens of thousands of people, it said. Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said in a social media post that another alleged Saudi coalition attack in the Lahj province, in Yemen's southwest, targeted buses and other vehicles. He said there were unspecified casualties. Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on either of the purported attacks. The coalition said Sunday that it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched at Saudi Arabia's western Red Sea coast. CBS/AFP U.S. discussing training Syrian armed forces, Reuters reports The United States is discussing plans to train Syrian soldiers to conduct demining work, five people familiar with the matter told the Reuters news agency. The plan could see a small number of U.S. troops return to Syria as soon as next year if it is adopted. The proposal is for a multinational training mission – made up of 15 countries including the U.K., France and Saudi Arabia –  to focus on demining and ordnance disposal. It would be the first time since 2024 that U.S. troops had trained Syrian counterparts. The U.S. State Department told Reuters that Washington welcomed having a partner in the Syrian capital, President Ahmed al-Sharaa , who is committed to combating the terror group ISIS. U.S. officials would need to do due diligence to screen all prospective Syrian recipients of the training before any funding is dedicated to the prospective project, two of the sources told Reuters. Iranian singer convicted of "outraging public decency" lashed 74 times for performing without hijab An Iranian singer has been lashed 74 times after being convicted of the crime of "outraging public decency" for performing without wearing the hijab head covering that is mandatory for women in the country. Parastoo Ahmadi was lashed Monday over her 2024 live-streamed YouTube concert, according to her attorney, who was quoted by the reformist Iranian newspaper Emtemad. The lawyer told Emtemad that Ahmadi and four members of her production team presented themselves to provincial authorities in the holy city of Qom Monday as required after their sentences were upheld in September by a local criminal court. The criminal court in Qom upheld the convictions for "outraging public decency" citing "immoral" content posted online during Ahmadi's performance in December 2024, which went viral in Iran. In addition to the 74 lashes, Parastoo and eight members of her team were also sentenced to a two-year ban on travel out of the country and a two-year ban on all "artistic activity." Parastoo performed her concert in the Dayr-Gachin Caravanserai - an ancient site along the Silk Road route in Iran. It included themes of nationalism and popular uprising, and saw her openly flout both the Islamic Republic's dress code and a long-standing ban on women singing in public. Netanyahu warns against downplaying "grave threats" facing Israel Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's now-caretaker prime minister, said Monday that Israel is still facing "serious and grave threats," and he warned of the dangers of downplaying them. He spoke shortly after his domestic political opponent, Gadi Eisenkot, said he saw no immediate threat posed by Iran that would warrant military action before a new Israeli government is formed to oust Netanyahu. "Anyone who belittles or downplays these immediate, serious and grave threats surrounding us does so for political reasons," Netanyahu said at a briefing in Israel's parliament, in which he called for a unity government, as Eisenkot attempts to form a new ruling coalition. CBS/AFP Netanyahu foe trying to form new Israeli government says no "immediate threat" requiring action against Iran Gadi Eisenkot, the Israeli politician trying to form a new government to oust current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the wake of national elections, has said he sees no "immediate threat" from Iran requiring military action. Speaking at a meeting of his party, Yashar, Monday, he said: "I see no direct and immediate threat from Iran today that would require Israel to act before a new government is formed." He added that "the gravest threat Iran poses" comes from its stockpile on enriched uranium: "That is where we need to focus." Netanyahu has appeared keen to go on the offensive against Iran again. Sources familiar with the matter told CBS News last week that Israel and the U.S. were considering a new assault on the country . Eisenkot recently said Netanyahu should not make any big national security decisions in the transition period following Israel's election, in which Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority, and that the now-caretaker prime minister should avoid "dangerous steps that can wait for the swearing in of a new government." Iran seeks $290 billion in damages against the U.S. Iran is due $290 billion from the United States to cover damages inflicted both during, and long before the war launched jointly by the U.S. and Israel almost nine months ago, Iran's judiciary authorities say. Iranian courts have demanded the U.S. pay the sum, a judiciary official said Monday. "We have secured court rulings in domestic courts awarding $290 billion in damages against the Americans," said Hassan Abdolianpour, head of the judiciary's center for lawyers, according to state television. He also said several lawsuits had been filed against Persian Gulf Arab nations for "allowing their territory to be used by America to launch attacks against Iran." According to state TV, the damages cover U.S. actions going back decades. On Monday, state broadcaster IRIB said several U.S.-linked commercial ships had been seized and that part of the compensation owed to Iran would be settled through the seizures, without giving further details. CBS/AFP Lebanon denounces Israeli military official's visit to school in south Lebanese officials have denounced a visit by an Israeli military spokesperson to a school in an Israeli-occupied area of southern Lebanon. As Lebanon marked its independence day on Sunday, the Israeli military's Arabic-language spokesperson Ella Waweya shared a video on social media showing her outside a school in Debl, a Christian village, and then standing in front of a classroom full of children. The village is located inside a wide swath of southern Lebanon that Israel has occupied and declared a "security zone" after the latest war erupted with Hezbollah in March. The zone covers a strip of southern Lebanon along the border and stretches about six miles into Lebanese territory. Debl is among a number of Christian-majority villages near the border where many residents have refused to leave despite Israeli military orders to evacuate. Cut off from the rest of Lebanon, they are largely dependent on humanitarian aid. "During my last visit to south Lebanon, I was amazed by the beauty of the land and the villages which have paid a heavy price due to their exploitation ... by a terrorist organization," Waweya said, referring to the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam denounced Israel for "dragging students into a military and propaganda display." "An occupying power has no right to exploit our children to embellish the image of its occupation or impose its dominance over our people in the south," he added. Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war in March with rocket fire at Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion. Lebanon says Israeli attacks since then have killed more than 4,300 people. CBS/AFP Iran says will use "all available means" to counter U.S. blockade Iran said Monday it would use all means at its disposal to counter a U.S. naval blockade imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz. "We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter U.S. aggression," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in his weekly press briefing. Soon after the war broke out, the Strait of Hormuz became the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies. In response, the U.S. imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran. "You should bear in mind that what the Americans have described as economic sanctions, an economic blockade and a naval blockade undoubtedly constitutes an act of military aggression against Iran," said Baqaei. "Under these circumstances, Iran is entitled, pursuant to Article 51 of the U.N. Charter, to use any means at its disposal to defend itself." Iran has said Hormuz could be open within two days but only if Washington agreed to its list of demands , which include the lifting of the blockade. Houthi media say 4 dead in Saudi attack on key port city Houthi media said Monday that a Saudi attack killed four people and wounded 18 in Yemen's key port city of Hodeida. The Iran-backed fighters, who control large swathes of Yemen including Hodeida, are battling a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognized government. The strike targeted a building belonging to Yemen's Public Telecommunications Corporation, the Houthis' Almasirah television channel wrote on X. Riyadh didn't immediately comment on the report. It came a day after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward the kingdom's western Red Sea coast. That region is home to major oil installations that Houthi fighters have attacked in recent weeks, along with strikes on airports and military sites. Yemen, which has been embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the U.S.-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unraveled. Since then, hostilities have left more than 1,600 people dead and more than 300,000 displaced in the country, the poorest on the Arabian Peninsula, according to the latest U.N. data. Houthis say Saudi strike on Yemen capital wounds 6 Houthi rebels in Yemen reported an airstrike early Sunday in the capital, Sanaa. A spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry, Anees al-Asbahi, said the strike hit a fuel station operated by the state-run oil company and wounded six workers. The strike also damaged the company's building, al-Asbahi said. The Red Sea port city of Mokha also came under fire on Sunday, Houthi-run television reported, as did the Haifan district in the southwestern province of Taiza. The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia for the airstrikes but didn't report any casualties from them. Trump says Iran launched more drones and missiles in past week "than at any time for over a year" President Trump on Sunday acknowledged that Iran "has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but he added: "Don't worry, they've all been knocked down, and done no damage." In a post on Truth Social, the president linked the midterm elections — in which Democrats won majorities in both chambers of Congress — to the escalation in the war with Iran. "As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran, which has killed 81,000 protestors as of today, will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," Mr. Trump said. Higher fuel prices triggered by the war caused economic concerns for Americans, and top Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, have partly attributed GOP election defeats to the war with Iran. Mr. Trump on Sunday said voters "didn't understand" what their votes meant and called the election "very 'strange.'" "Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won't let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," he said. "Too bad the Voters didn't understand this before they pulled the trigger, but the whole Election was very 'strange.'" Athlete swims Strait of Hormuz to raise awareness of Iran war's toll on wildlife British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh has swum in the North Pole and Antarctica to draw attention to environmental causes. But battling freezing waters and extreme conditions hasn't prepared him for his latest challenge: swimming the Strait of Hormuz while tankers are attacked and blown up nearby. Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days this week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how the war with Iran threatens the area's habitat and wildlife. Wearing only swimming trunks, goggles and a cap bearing the U.N. logo, the athlete started from the Musandam Peninsula, on the southern tip of the strait, and ended by rounding the Cape of Hormuz, completing about 9.3 miles in total. Pugh is believed to be the first person to undertake a long-distance swim there since the war started. The swimmer said that minutes after he entered the water on Monday, he heard two loud explosions that rocked the sea. Read more here . Iran holds talks with Qatari mediators Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks," without providing details. Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran to end the war have stalled in recent months. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said, however, that ongoing talks in the region must be "given a chance" and that the ongoing U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "must be lifted rationally." "Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state television. "At the same time, we have always affirmed our readiness for dialogue, just as we are ready to defend ourselves." Iran's conditions have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports. CBS/AFP Trump says he wants to make "permanent" deal with Iranian regime President Trump said Saturday that he wants to make a "permanent" deal with Iran that will prevent the country from gaining a nuclear weapon in the future. "What I'm doing is I'm going to make it so that if we have an incompetent president in four years or 15 years or 20 years, I'm going to make a deal that is going to be permanent," Mr. Trump told Fox News in a phone interview on Saturday. "I'm not going to let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon." Mr. Trump said he's never "cared too much about the regime" leading Iran, and that he has "taken out two regimes already," though he declined to specify further. Former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in the initial strikes on Iran that began the war in February 2026. His son Mojtaba Khamenei has held the title ever since. Mr. Trump said Iranian officials have been "very, very difficult" to make a deal with. "I mean, we make a deal and then they break the deal the next day," Mr. Trump said. articles.title: Trump says Huang is not a national security risk. Why are others so concerned?
articles.summary: When news broke Monday that Nvidia had reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO less than two weeks after he resigned amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs — including one with a woman suspected of spying for China — President Trump was quick to reassure the public that "the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security." "People say, 'Is it a threat to have him?' No, it's a threat to lose him," Trump told CNBC shortly after the announcement . But not everyone agrees . Before Huang resigned, the Trump administration's own intelligence officials reportedly identified Alice Huang — the Chinese-born leader of a Southeast Asian company called Megaspeed — as a Chinese intelligence asset who kept in touch with Beijing's top spy agency for more than a year while she targeted the Nvidia chief. Why does this matter? Without government authorization, U.S. export controls prohibit Nvidia from selling certain advanced AI microchips — the chips that have powered the artificial intelligence boom — directly to China, America's main AI competitor. But during a period when Jensen and Alice Huang were seen dining and socializing together , Megaspeed wound up buying billions of dollars' worth of those same Nvidia chips. And Megaspeed not only has ties to Beijing . It's actually under federal investigation for potentially smuggling advanced Nvidia semiconductors out of the U.S. and into China. Jensen Huang during the Nvidia GTC global AI conference in San Jose, Calif., on March 17, 2026. Carlos Barria/Reuters As a result, Huang's reinstatement triggered immediate bipartisan backlash. Outgoing Republican Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska accused Huang of being "compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy" and said "Nvidia should have moved on" without him. "Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high end computer chips sales to China," Bacon wrote on social media . "We cannot say we want to win the AI race and then give China our best technology. We need sunlight on who is responsible." Jensen Huang was compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy. Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the Administration’s inexplicable desire to save Huang. Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high end computer chips sales to China. We cannot say we… — Rep. Don Bacon 🇺🇸✈️🏍️⭐️🎖️ (@RepDonBacon) November 23, 2026 Sen. John Cornyn — another retiring Republican lawmaker — questioned Trump's seemingly cavalier attitude toward Huang and China. "No national security risk?" Cornyn posted . "Based on what?" On Monday, Trump took credit for Huang's return, saying he had spoken directly to Nvidia's board. "I convinced them," the president told CNBC . "I made the deal." The U.S. position on chip sales to China has seesawed over the last 18 months. In April 2025, the Trump administration imposed its first major restrictions on AI semiconductor sales outside the U.S., toughening rules created by the Biden administration. But after several meetings between Trump and Huang — who consistently lobbied for letting chip companies do business with China — the administration eventually approved sales of Nvidia's second-most-powerful chip to Beijing. At the same time, " advisers to Trump told him on at least two occasions that U.S. intelligence had uncovered Ms. Huang's links to the Chinese spy agency and that she was in a close relationship with Mr. Huang while he was still running Nvidia," according to the New York Times . But Trump "downplayed the concerns" and refused to intervene because he "regarded Mr. Huang as a valuable ally and Nvidia as essential to the health of the American economy and stock market," U.S. officials with direct knowledge of the briefings told the paper. Meanwhile, After Jensen stepped down, Trump went on to muse about his return and question whether Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, denying that anyone in his government had ever told him that. "I don't know that she is a spy," the president told reporters last week . "Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that's a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she's a spy." On Sunday, Trump called for Huang's return on social media. The New York Times reported that it came after "several days of maneuvering to provide the company's board with assurances that Mr. Huang was not facing criminal charges and did not pose a national security risk." That maneuvering reportedly included directing Vice President JD Vance, who has close ties to Silicon Valley, to speak with both Huang and Nvidia's board. President Trump and Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, interact during the U.S.-Saudi Investment Forum in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 19, 2025. Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters On Monday, the board announced that it had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang. Trump responded by calling Huang "a Great Patriot and National Treasure" and insisting that "the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." In the same post, Trump added that "NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security." But an internal probe is unlikely to satisfy Congress. Huang is already set to deliver closed-door testimony on Dec. 1 before three congressional committees led by Republicans — and Democrats have signaled that they will keep investigating the issue when they take control of the House and Senate next year. On Monday, Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona accused Trump of "selling out our national security to keep the stock market high." Another Democrat, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, said on social media that "this is the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected." "There are serious national security concerns being raised about Jensen Huang that should not be papered over by this administration or the Nvidia board," Pritzker added. The president is a significant investor in Nvidia stock. Last week, the Washington Post reported that by August 2026, Trump held a $13 million to $62 million stake in Nvidia — up from as little as $615,000 at the end of 2024. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also accused the commerce department, led by Howard Lutnick, of stalling efforts by the treasury, defense and state departments, as well as the U.S. trade representative, to block chip sales to Megaspeed. "Commerce has the pen," Bessent said on CNBC earlier this month . "You will have to ask them about their internal processes." Lutnick's former firm Cantor Fitzgerald — now led by his sons — has business relationships with Southeast Asian data centers, leading lawmakers on both sides of the aisle to question "whether Lutnick compromised national security to make money for his family," according to the Guardian . Lutnick should have taken "the threats of communist China more seriously," Republican Sen. Tom Cotton of Arkansas told the Wall Street Journal last week . Congressional Democrats have said they plan to investigate Lutnick in 2027. articles.title: Stocks surge as Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia sparks stunning rally
articles.summary: Stocks soared on Monday as investors cheered Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. It marked a major rebound on Monday as buyers stepped back in for the holiday-shortened week after a bruising sell-off. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose nearly 5% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) jumped more than 1,500 points to recover by 3.3% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) rallied 6.7%. Nvidia stock soared more than 30% after the AI chipmaker announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair Harvey Jones said. Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO > The move came after President Trump renewed his call to reinstate the chipmaker's founder, Jensen Huang, as CEO amid a series of controversies. articles.title: Trump tells Army it needs court approval to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
articles.summary: President Donald Trump on Monday said he will defer to a federal appeals court on whether the administration moves ahead with plans to detonate several tons of degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant. The detonation of 68 barrels of lead azide was initially planned for Friday, but the Army has since changed the date three times following an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects. They had planned for a detonation on Wednesday, saying the weather was most favorable that day. The Army had no immediate comment when asked about the president’s social media post. Environmentalists sued last week in an effort to stop the detonation, winning a stay from the appeals court pending a decision on the validity of an emergency permit approved by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency that cleared the way for the operation. Trump says he'd blame incoming governor for any ‘death or destruction’ “I feel the proper course is to get rid of this longterm problem but, at the same time, have ordered the Military not to do so until such time as the Eighth Circuit agrees that we can go forward," Trump posted. If incoming Gov.-elect Rob Sand and the court don’t agree, Trump said the administration will have no choice but to not proceed with the planned detonation, adding that he would hold the incoming governor responsible for “any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation.” Sand said in a social media post on Sunday that because of previous decisions that have already been made, “No good options exist and the situation is more dangerous and unpredictable than it ever should have been.” He questioned why a contract to remove the explosive risk was canceled, why nothing was done and “why we are rushing to demolition now in late November.” “The safety of Iowans should be the top priority of everyone involved,” he said. “All relevant federal, state and local government resources should be focused on protecting everyone that could be impacted.” Residents left in limbo as they prepare for detonation Some residents near Middletown, where the ammunition plant is located, have been sealing their windows and doors as a precaution to keep out any lead dust that might result from the detonation. Others who live farther away were raising concern on social media about the possible paths that the plume could take depending on shifts in the wind. Officials acknowledge that lead is toxic and have recommended that people stay indoors whenever the detonation happens and clean off outdoor surfaces with water afterwards to limit exposure to any lead particles. Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson said the detonation must take place “so we can move on with our lives.” “Improper storage and disposal is where things go wrong,” he said on social media. Rachel Rintelmann, an attorney with the environmental group Earthjustice, said Monday she could not yet say what impact Trump’s call for the military to stand down may have on the case. “What I can say is that this post only adds further confusion to a situation that has already caused chaos in the lives of impacted communities,” Rintelmann said. “The people of Iowa deserve better than this.” Army says plans are aimed at avoiding something worse In court filings over the weekend, Army Col. Aaron Teller, a munitions emergency response specialist, explained that less liquid inside the barrels means the solution inside is more susceptible to freezing, which increases the sensitivity of the crystals that have formed around the inside of the rim and underside of the lids. “Even a small amount of friction can break the crystal formation, causing an explosive chain reaction,” he said in his declaration to the court. In March, staff at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant found several dozen barrels of degraded lead azide, which is used in munitions production. Crystallization of the material created an unstable and dangerous situation, prompting the Army to assemble experts in munitions chemistry, engineering and environmental safety to come up with a plan. According to EPA documents, alternatives such as neutralizing and decomposing the drums’ contents with other chemicals were considered. But officials said handling the drums would increase the probability of an accidental, fatal detonation. The environmental groups disagreed, arguing in their court filings that other alternatives were not fully considered. They also criticized officials for not sharing more information with the public. Officials contend that the risk of an uncontrolled explosion is growing, particularly as temperatures drop. They said there is a risk that the chemicals may explode as temperatures are expected to drop below 30 degrees Fahrenheit (-1 Celsius) in the coming days. articles.title: Medicare for All was once a long shot. Now, parts of it are in Democrats' agenda.
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — What were once long-shot ideas around universal healthcare — championed by Sen. Bernie Sanders' Medicare for All — have suddenly been catapulted to the forefront of the Democratic agenda for the new Congress in January. The party in its first 100 days is planning swift action on legislation to reverse recent Medicaid cuts that threaten to leave millions of people without care and to revive tax breaks that help people who buy insurance through the Affordable Care Act . But it's also becoming clear that the Democrats have far more ambitious healthcare goals as they prepare to take charge on Jan. 3, 2027. Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, on track to become House speaker, announced his intentions to take steps toward Medicare for All in a post-midterm election speech that stunned health advocates. He listed proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age below 65, add dental, vision and hearing aid benefits, and open up healthcare to children as part of the incoming majority's plans — all aspects of Medicare for All. Sanders, a Vermont independent who caucuses with Democrats, unveiled his push for portions of Medicare for All as he takes over the chairmanship of the Senate health committee. And even former President Barack Obama encouraged newly elected Democrats to go beyond the ACA, also known as Obamacare, which was among his signature accomplishments in office. "We got the ACA done, which was wonderful," Obama said, according to a transcript of his remarks to the incoming Democrats at the Capitol. "But I was very explicit at the time. This is a starter home. It is not the answer," he said. "You should push further and get more." After a change election that ousted Republicans in a rebuke of President Donald Trump's party, Democratic leaders are eager to use their incoming wide majorities in the House and the Senate to deliver on their campaign promises, particularly healthcare affordability. The details are still taking shape, and there almost certainly will be pushback from moderate and centrist Democrats who helped win the majorities, especially regarding the costs of any healthcare expansion. But Democratic leaders appear increasingly confident that proposals to expand healthcare are no longer far-flung liberal ideas but are basics that voters who sent them to Washington expect from their government. "It's been an ongoing conversation over the last several months, about how we acknowledge the urgency of the moment on healthcare and that it can't just be going back to restoring what was," said Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., who has been in talks with Jeffries about moving the legislation forward. Voters want more government action on healthcare About 6 in 10 voters nationally said the federal government should play a bigger role in helping Americans get healthcare than it does now, according to The AP Voter Poll , a survey of more than 100,000 midterm voters. The same number said they are "very concerned" about the cost of healthcare, according to the survey. Sanders, who has advocated for healthcare essentially since he arrived in Congress more than 30 years ago, is now seen as an elder statesman on the issue for a new generation of lawmakers, including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. Jeffries, who had been an early co-sponsor of Medicare for All but backed away once he became House Democratic leader after the 2022 election, recently namechecked Sanders as the "O.G." whose committee will be among those tackling the issue. "We're going to begin very early on in the new Congress by working to reverse the Medicaid cuts and working to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits," Jeffries said at a post-election conference of Democrats in Denver. "And then we've got to go further to make sure that we don't just fix what's broken but that we build upon what we need to do," he said, as a heckler tried to shout him down. Jeffries went on, "I think we've got to lower the age of eligibility as it relates to Medicare. I think we've got to make sure that we cover hearing, vision and dental, and we got to make sure that every child in America can be able to see a doctor with high-quality, affordable healthcare." Progressives were thrilled. Jeffries had essentially outlined the first year of Medicare for All's multiyear phase-in plan. "We had a sense that he was positively inclined," said Jayapal, who is also a past chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, "but he just went ahead and did it." Trump has the power of veto but also a penchant for deals Trump has promised to use the power of the presidential veto to swat back the Democratic agenda. But as Trump takes stock of his final two years in office with Democrats in charge of Congress, he has also indicated the potential for dealmaking with Jeffries and Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer. "They're all smart," Trump said about the fellow New Yorkers at a news conference on Friday, his first since the midterm election blowout. "They're going to send things my way, and I'm going to veto them," he said. "But I think after a month or so they're going to send things and I'm going to say, 'I'm going to veto — unless you want to do this and this and this.'" Trump suggested that after years of his own Republican Party's efforts on healthcare — largely attempts to repeal and replace Obamacare — perhaps he could find something better with the Democrats. "There's a real possibility that we'll get a lot of great things done, especially on healthcare," he said. "Now, can it be what they want? No, but it can be a combination of what we all want. And we could end up with great healthcare in our country." Democratic Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, who aligns with Sanders on this and other issues, recently posted imagery of "TrumpCare," a golden insurance card, enticing the president to consider a universal healthcare system. Senate could prove an obstacle to their plans With their large House majority , Democrats should be able to quickly pass their initial bills to reverse the Medicaid cuts and restore the ACA tax credits, but the outcome in the Senate is less certain. Democrats will have a 56-seat majority in the 100-member Senate, but most bills in the Senate require a 60-vote threshold to advance over a filibuster, if Republicans try to block the legislation. And Trump's veto threats loom. But healthcare advocates are pushing Democrats to try anyway and see what happens. "Why bother? That's what members of Congress are elected to do — to try and try hard," said Brad Woodhouse, a seasoned strategist and executive director of the advocacy group Protect Our Care, "and if they fail, to try again." articles.title: Dual storms are forecast to snarl Thanksgiving travel from coast to coast
articles.summary: Millions of Americans hitting the road and skies for Thanksgiving could run into storms on both coasts, including one that could last through Thanksgiving Day. On the West Coast, the National Weather Service has issued a coastal flood warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines from Monday through Thursday afternoon, as the year's highest "king tides" coincide with an incoming storm. A coastal storm is also bringing heavy rain and gusty winds from the mid-Atlantic to New England, which started Sunday night and continued Monday morning. Forecasters are tracking a potentially strong nor'easter for Thanksgiving Day, and an atmospheric river on the West Coast. "Each of these storms has the potential to trigger major weather delays at major Northeast and West Coast hubs," the Weather Channel said . Weather hasn't been the only problem facing travelers. Delta Air Lines resolved an outage that caused delays nationwide Sunday, marking the third major disruption to U.S. air travel in nine days. AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30, including 72.9 million by car and 5.96 million on domestic flights. Monday: Heavy rain in the Northeast Forecasters are growing more confident that another storm will hit the Northeast on Thanksgiving, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and flooding along the coast. The National Hurricane Center said Saturday that it was unlikely to become a tropical or subtropical storm. In New York City, heavy rain started Sunday and has persisted into Monday, city emergency officials said .  The National Weather Service in New York said early Monday to expect 1 to 2 inches of rain, with more in places, and wind gusts of 35 to 45 mph, possibly near 50 mph on the coast. Flooding along the shore could be widespread, with major flooding possible in the most vulnerable spots on Long Island's south shore, the agency said. The storm's timing and track could still change. New York City Emergency Management said gusty winds Monday could slow flights. In Florida, more than 16 inches of rain fell near Cocoa Beach over three days, according to AccuWeather, and the St. Johns River near Cocoa hit 18.6 feet Friday, breaking a record set in 1953. Flooding along the river is expected to linger past Thanksgiving. Tuesday and Wednesday: Atmospheric river in the West, storms in the Southeast Map of atmospheric river forecast to affect California leading up to Thanksgiving Day. AccuWeather A strong Pacific storm is forecast to hit from Northern California to Washington state starting Tuesday, with rain reaching the Northwest Monday night. The greatest impacts are expected Tuesday and Wednesday, with a risk of flooding and mudslides. Heavy rain, strong winds and mountain snow could cause significant delays along Interstate 5 between Seattle and San Francisco and on mountain routes including I-80. Airports in Seattle and San Francisco could see delays. "Drivers along I-5 should prepare for heavy rain that can reduce visibility and leave water collecting on the roadway," AccuWeather meteorologist Haley Taylor said. "Travelers heading into the Sierra will face a different challenge, with heavy snow potentially making mountain routes difficult or impassable." A second, potentially windier storm could strike the same area Wednesday, with the heaviest rain spreading to most of the West Coast on Thursday, the Weather Channel said. The National Weather Service office in Reno said the storms will bring fresh snow to the Sierra Nevada, with periods of difficult travel. In the San Francisco Bay Area, the storms coincide with potentially record-breaking king tides, the year's highest tides. The National Weather Service has a coastal flood warning in effect until 4 p.m. PT Thursday and calls Tuesday and Wednesday an "extreme" risk for flooding along the bay shoreline, and a high surf warning covers Wednesday on the Pacific coast. The agency said the storm will coincide with the king tides, potentially making flooding worse during Thanksgiving travel. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said Sunday city departments are coordinating and "deploying resources" for the storms and high tides. He previously warned of potentially record tides in an X post Saturday. “We went through the forecast for next week, and we are anticipating high tides and rain that this city has never seen before,” he said “This is extremely serious, and we are acting accordingly at the city level. We are going to encourage every resident and business owner to take this extremely seriously. In Marin County, Southern Marin Fire District has urged residents and businesses to "take action now" and prepare for possible road closures and travel disruptions. In the Southeast, heavy rain and thunderstorms could hit Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday, one of the busiest travel days of the year. AccuWeather said Wednesday could bring some of the most widespread weather-related travel disruptions before Thanksgiving, particularly in the Southeast, with airline delays expected to expand in Orlando and Miami from Tuesday to Wednesday and in Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday. The National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center has warned of flooding rain along the coastal Carolinas on Wednesday. Delays at those hubs could ripple across the country. Thanksgiving Day: Possible major storm in the Northeast Forecasters are increasingly confident that another storm will form off the Southeast coast late Wednesday and move up the East Coast on Thanksgiving, bringing heavy rain and strong winds from the mid-Atlantic to New England. The National Weather Service in Boston called it a "potentially significant coastal storm" for Thanksgiving into Friday, with gusts along the coast possibly topping 50 mph. Very high tides could also bring coastal flooding, the agency said. Interior parts of the Northeast and the Appalachians could see some snow or ice. The storm arrives as king tides continue on both coasts around Tuesday's full moon, which could worsen coastal flooding, the Weather Channel said. Interior parts of the Northeast and the Appalachians could see some snow or ice. AccuWeather said a brief period of wet snow or sleet is possible in northern New York and New England later Thursday. That could be a problem for the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which is set to start at 8:30 a.m. Thursday. The parade's giant balloons can't fly if sustained winds top 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph, Fox Weather reported . Forecasters say the storm's exact track and timing could still shift. The weekend after Thanksgiving The National Weather Service expects the East Coast storm to weaken and move away, though windy conditions and some rain or snow showers could linger in parts of New England and the eastern Great Lakes into the weekend. Another storm could form in the East during the busy return weekend, while more Pacific storms could hit the West Coast. The Sunday after Thanksgiving is typically one of the busiest travel days of the year. Forecasters advise travelers to check forecasts for both their departure and arrival cities, and to keep an eye on flight status before heading to the airport. articles.title: U.S. intelligence chief warns Americans to brace for more tech outages
articles.summary: People should prepare for more technology outages and disruptions to digital services , according to US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. In an interview with CNN, Mr Clayton warned that decades-old systems are undergoing urgent upgrades to improve security against emerging cyber threats like autonomous artificial intelligence agents. “The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cyber security , and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road,” Mr Clayton said. “You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.” His comments come after a series of major tech failures that caused outages to critical services and digital infrastructure. These have included a global Microsoft outage – which knocked out emails for governments, doctor surgeries and businesses – as well as a communications failure with the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) that grounded flights for several hours. Mr Clayton said investment was needed to improve cyber security and protect increasingly sophisticated and exposed networks. “As part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service," Mr Clayton said. "That ​is ⁠going to happen." Jay Clayton, director of US National Intelligence, speaks during an investor summit in New York City, US, on 20 October, 2026 (Reuters) Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reiterated the warning on CBS, saying that there could be some issues with updates introduced by banks to protect against AI . “The patches may cause a glitch,” he said. “I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency.” The White House recently moved to overhaul its cyber security leadership, naming Kirsten Davies as the new National Cyber Director after Sean Cairncross stepped aside. In her new role she will oversee cyber security policy and strategy across the federal government. "Our nation stands in the crossroad of analog, digital, and quantum technologies, our American way of living increasingly interconnected," she wrote in a post on X. "Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come… But only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future." articles.title: DOJ admits in court that Trump admin. deported U.S. citizen to Mexico
articles.summary: Court filings recount how border patrol agent Robert Gil Jr consulted records from Mexico that listed a Mexican birthplace for Brian Morales. Photograph: Dominic Gwinn/Middle East Images/AFP/Getty Images The Trump administration recently admitted in federal court that it deported a US citizen to Mexico after American authorities incorrectly concluded he was an undocumented immigrant. Attorneys for the US justice department made that admission on Friday while requesting the dismissal of a lawsuit for damages that the deported man – Brian José Morales García of Austin, Texas – has been pursuing against the federal government. Morales García’s case took that turn as the White House has faced bipartisan criticism for the aggressive mass deportation campaign pursued by Donald Trump throughout his second presidency – widely seen as a factor in the electoral battering his Republican party suffered during the 3 November midterms, costing it control of Congress . The Denver-born, Mexico-raised Morales García was riding with his boss to his job as an air-conditioning installation technician on 3 April when they were pulled over by state and local officers near Fredericksburg, Texas. Related: They went out to celebrate at a Memphis bar. Then, ICE descended Morales García was his boss’s passenger and did not have his identification on him. The 25-year-old also told the officers that he had his birth certificate and social security card at home, but they didn’t believe him – so they called immigration agents, who detained Morales García. Court filings recount how Robert Gil Jr, a US Customs and Border Protection agent, consulted records from Mexico that listed a Mexican birthplace for Morales García. Gil Jr also accused Morales García of saying he was born in Mexico and observed that he only spoke in Spanish, according to court records. Morales García was deported on 7 April, with the Trump administration later accusing him in a media statement of being in the country illegally. Morales García’s attorneys sued on 1 May, maintaining that he had falsely said he entered the US illegally and signed papers for a rapid deportation in response to threats of imprisonment by agents. His lawsuit, which seeks an unspecified amount of money, also contended that family and friends tried to deliver documents proving his US citizenship before this deportation. But those efforts were unduly rebuffed, Morales García’s lawsuit said. The Trump administration denied Morales García’s assertions, saying on Friday that he went to Mexico voluntarily and therefore lacked any basis to sue the federal government for damages. Nonetheless, in court filings on Friday, the administration conceded that Morales García “was permitted entry” back into the US on 30 August after it reviewed “information concerning plaintiff’s place of birth”. “Plaintiff is a dual citizen of the United States and Mexico,” Justin Simmons, the US attorney for the western district of Texas, wrote in a court filing first reported by the Texas Tribune . Related: Judge says ICE ‘made a mockery of court orders’ with instant re-arrest policy Americans are not required to carry proof of citizenship when going about their daily business. Lawyers across the US have seen cases such as Morales García’s, which begin after an encounter with local authorities demonstrate how those officials are generally not aware of the nuances of immigration policy. Texas’s public safety department is among many US state and local agencies that collaborate with federal immigration authorities under their 287(g) program . The judge presiding over Morales García’s lawsuit, Robert Lee Pitman, did not immediately rule on the Trump administration’s request on Friday to dismiss the case. The lawsuit also named unspecified local and state Texas law enforcement officers as defendants. An October 2025 report by ProPublica found that immigration agents had detained more than 170 US citizens during the first nine months of Trump’s second presidency. Meanwhile, the media statement incorrectly saying Morales García was in the US illegally is among several related to immigration enforcement under the Trump administration that has unraveled under scrutiny. A Guardian analysis published in July reviewed Trump administration press releases on 26 cases of cars allegedly being used to assault immigration enforcement agents – and nearly all were either disproven or dropped. articles.title: House GOP leadership races against clock as absences continue to derail final agenda
articles.summary: House Republicans have just three weeks left in session to advance their legislative priorities before Democrats take control of Congress in January, leaving a narrow window to push through an assortment of unfinished business. At the top of the list is reaching an agreement on a stopgap measure, known as a continuing resolution (CR), or passing all 12 appropriations bills before the Dec. 11 funding deadline to avert a government shutdown. Republicans also face pressure to get the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), permitting reform legislation, a farm bill and other items across the finish line. But it won’t be an easy task for Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) to wrangle his caucus, especially as he struggles to keep his own members in Washington long enough to get the work done. Attendance problems have already begun disrupting the House floor schedule. GOP leaders postponed a procedural rule vote Wednesday over absences and canceled Friday’s votes altogether. Twenty-one Republicans missed votes on Thursday morning, following 14 absences the previous day. Johnson will need near-unanimous support on any procedural rule if he decides to bring a bill to the floor via regular order, requiring most of his conference to be present as he juggles a razor-thin margin. The House this week took up bills under a fast-track process known as suspension of the rules, which requires a two-thirds majority for passage and is typically reserved for legislation with broad bipartisan support. Because those bills often attract significant Democratic backing, Republicans can afford absences without jeopardizing passage. Johnson called the attendance issue “a great frustration” and told reporters he plans to address it directly with members. He went a step further on Friday and urged his colleagues to show up and vote in a letter posted to the social platform X. “To state the obvious, barring any serious medical issue, we need every Republican to be here to faithfully complete our full two-year term,” he said. House lawmakers left Washington for Thanksgiving recess, leaving them with a little more than a week to address government funding after they return. House Appropriations Committee Chair Tom Cole (R-Okla.) told reporters that he wants to pass 12 appropriations bills and has little appetite for a CR. The three appropriations bills the House has passed so far — funding military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs, the State Department and agriculture and rural development — represent some of the lowest-hanging fruit. Johnson is sure to face much tougher resistance — both from Democrats and within his party — when the topic shifts to funding other agencies, including the departments of Homeland Security, Defense, and Health and Human Services. Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins (R-Maine), meanwhile, released text for all 12 bills negotiated by the upper chamber this month. Republicans on the Senate Appropriations Committee previously told The Hill there are still lots of moving pieces but that the end result is likely going to be some kind of short-term CR. Still, Cole said in a statement that he’s “used to long odds and tight timelines.” “Neither has ever deterred me from doing the work. A lame duck doesn’t have to leave full-year bills dead in the water. … The biggest disservice to the American people would be not to try. I refuse to let any opportunity available pass us by simply because some are already looking at the next Congress while this one still has votes to take,” Cole said. Rep. Nick LaLota (R-N.Y.), who serves on the House Appropriations Committee, told The Hill that “everything should be on the table to pass 12 appropriations bills.” Also on the GOP to-do list is the annual defense policy bill, which is facing an uphill climb in the Senate over its $1.15 trillion request. Senate Democrats blocked the upper chamber’s version of the bill back in July, citing President Trump’s handling of the Iran war. And any NDAA passed by the Senate must be reconciled with the House version, which passed the lower chamber in July. The House is also looking to take up a major bipartisan permitting reform bill that passed the Senate this week. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) wrote on X that the legislation would “cut red tape, create jobs, and lower costs for families,” and he urged the House to “finish the job” by sending the bill to Trump’s desk. The bill will likely pass the lower chamber, but the path to getting it across the finish line remains uncertain. Johnson could move it under regular order, where attendance issues could complicate passage of a rule. It’s unclear whether he has enough Democratic support to move it under suspension of the rules. Trump has also been pushing Congress to pass legislation that would reauthorize spending for food and agricultural programs, writing in a Truth Social post this week that “IT IS TIME TO DO IT AGAIN, and FAST.” “Our Great Farmers and Ranchers NEED and DESERVE certainty ahead of the 2027 planting season because FOOD SECURITY IS NATIONAL SECURITY! Congressional Republican Majorities, YOU MUST PASS A NEW FARM BILL DURING THE REMAINING DAYS OF CONGRESS. FARMERS AND RANCHERS ARE NOT INTERESTED IN FURTHER DELAYS,” Trump wrote. While the House passed its version in April, the Senate has yet to approve its own. Asked about the upcoming deadlines and GOP priorities on the table, Rep. Tim Burchett (R-Tenn.) said, “I'm not confident we’re going to do anything.” Rep. Tony Wied (R-Wis.) said that he’s “not sure” whether Republicans will be able to advance all of their items on the agenda and meet pressing deadlines. “We have attendance issues, so, I think on both sides, and so at this point I don't know. I think it'd be a good idea to, and try to get some of these things done, but at this point, I'm not sure,” Wied said. Some Republicans have been pressing their colleagues to prioritize attendance and ensure the party makes the most of its dwindling time in the majority. “There is no excuse for not showing up,” Rep. Ralph Norman (R-S.C.) said. “They ought to publish every name of everybody and every vote they don't take. Secondly, we're at a critical time in this country, and we ought to be up here every day.” Rep. Dan Newhouse (R-Wash.) said “there's a lot of things that are very urgent.” “Certainly the CR, it's expiring, but there's a lot of, I would classify, must-pass bills that people recognize,” Newhouse said. “So I'm hopeful that we can come together and do that. You know, I'm a very optimistic person. Being a farmer, you have to be. And I bring that same attitude here. Not naive to the fact that there's a lot of challenges. People have to show up, and we've got some absences. Well, that's a problem. But we've got — I think we're up to the task, and we’ll get the work done.” Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. articles.title: 马斯克承认SpaceX AI研发落后，出租算力比自研Grok更赚钱
articles.summary: SpaceX的人工智能业务正面临一个深层矛盾：靠向竞争对手出租算力获利，远比发展自有AI产品更赚钱。 据《纽约时报》报道， 马斯克已向员工坦承，公司在AI研发上正在落后，这使得将算力对外出租比用于自研产品更具商业价值。 Anthropic每月向SpaceX支付约31亿美元购买算力，谷歌每月支付约8亿美元，相关协议可能延续至2029年。SpaceX旗下AI部门SpaceXSI目前贡献了公司逾半数营收。 这一格局对AI竞争格局的影响不容忽视。 SpaceX正在为其最有力的竞争对手提供关键基础设施支撑，而自身的Grok等AI产品却在同期面临缩编压力。 晨星研究分析师Nicolas Owens向《纽约时报》表示："SpaceX目前通过出租算力赚到的钱，远超Grok所带来的收入。" 黄仁勋回归推动美股科技大涨，SpaceX早盘一度11%，随后有所回落，截至发稿上涨6.3%。 马斯克内部承认落后，GPU效益成考核核心 马斯克对公司AI竞争力的担忧已明确传导至内部管理层面。据《纽约时报》报道，他今年8月一度将一个内部工程师群组的名称临时改为 "因为无法竞争所以出售算力" （Sell compute because we can't compete）。 他还要求工程师就使用高价图形处理器（GPU）的必要性进行自我论证。在一条经该报审阅的内部消息中，马斯克写道： "归根结底，衡量竞争力的唯一标准是每块GPU的营收，而不是跑分。如果你无法负担GPU的成本，要么破产，要么变成一家算力租赁公司。去推动营收增长。" 多个AI项目遭裁撤，资源向Grok核心功能集中 内部压力已直接导致多条AI产品线收缩。 SpaceX于今年9月关闭了AI虚拟伴侣项目，同时将原本投入"Digital Optimus"AI工作者项目的工程师调配至Grok核心能力开发。此外，负责Grok Imagine图像与视频生成工具的60人团队也已解散。 这一系列调整表明，在资源有限的情况下，SpaceX正将有限的研发力量进一步集中，同时收缩探索性项目的投入。 基础设施优势突出，大规模扩张持续推进 尽管AI产品端承压，SpaceX在算力基础设施方面仍保持显著优势，并持续加大投入。 该公司于2024年仅用122天便建成了孟菲斯大型数据中心，近期又宣布计划在亚利桑那州和德克萨斯州投资740亿美元新建数据中心。 马斯克本人在公开场合对Anthropic的需求表示欢迎。他在《纽约时报》DealBook峰会上表示， Anthropic极有可能继续租用SpaceX的算力，且有意大幅增加采购规模。 竞争悖论：为对手输血，同时谋求赶超 SpaceX当前的商业模式构成一个显著的战略悖论：通过向Anthropic和谷歌出售算力获取丰厚收益，但这两家公司恰恰是马斯克希望在AI领域超越的竞争对手。 这笔收入为SpaceX提供了可观的现金流，也支撑着其大规模基础设施扩张计划，但与此同时，也在客观上强化了竞争对手的技术能力。 Anthropic与谷歌的相关协议均设有90天提前终止条款，双方均可据此退出。这意味着SpaceX依赖外部客户的营收结构存在一定的稳定性风险，尤其是在竞争对手自建或转用其他算力来源的情况下。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 黄仁勋回归“比肥皂剧精彩”！华尔街争论他是否“大到不能解雇”、英伟达董事会是否向资本低头
articles.summary: 英伟达董事会宣布黄仁勋辞职仅11天后便一致决定恢复其职务，这场戏剧性反转引发华尔街热议，也将创始人权力、公司治理与政治干预企业决策的争议推至台前。 美东时间11月23日周一，英伟达宣布，董事会一致决定即刻恢复黄仁勋的总裁、CEO及董事职务。该司称，在与黄仁勋进行一系列讨论和会面后，董事会对其坦诚程度及领导公司能力感到满意。同时，董事会征询了美国政府高层意见，据此认定黄仁勋复职不会带来国家安全风险。董事会主席琼斯表示，黄仁勋是领导英伟达的合适人选，他回归符合股东、员工、合作伙伴和客户的利益。 这一决定与董事会此前的公开表态形成鲜明反差。将近一周前、17日上周二，在英伟达公布强劲财报后的业绩电话会上，琼斯曾表示，黄仁勋是自愿离职，董事会已一致接受其辞职，无意恢复他的CEO职务。本周一英伟达宣布黄仁勋复职后不久，美国总统特朗普公开表示，董事会作出了“正确且恰当的决定”，并称他推动了黄仁勋回归。 对于英伟达董事会短短六天后的180度大转向，有投资者直言“比肥皂剧还精彩”，也有人认为，黄仁勋对英伟达的重要性已达到“大到不能被解雇”的程度。 从英伟达股价周一大涨的反应看，市场欢迎黄仁勋回归，认为这有助于消除英伟达领导层变动及其对AI产业链融资支持的疑虑。但公司治理专家质疑董事会是否经过充分审查，批评者则担心政治压力凌驾于董事会独立决策之上。围绕这场复职风波，争论已不只是黄仁勋个人去留，而是英伟达究竟能否在创始人影响力、股东利益与国家安全责任之间维持制度约束。 华尔街：黄仁勋回归为何如此重要？ Interactive Brokers首席策略师Steve Sosnick称：“确实有很多人希望他回来……这在某种程度上说明，黄仁勋已经重要到不能被解雇。” Lemanik高级投资组合经理Andrea Scauri则用一句“比肥皂剧还精彩”形容这场风波。 他指出，黄仁勋回归消除了市场对英伟达是否会继续支持其投资企业的疑虑，尤其是通过债务和股权投资支持的企业。此前承压的新兴云服务商（neocloud）杠杆较高，黄仁勋回归有助于消除这一市场板块面临的很大一部分不确定性。 不过，并非所有华尔街人士都认为股价上涨意味着风险已经解除。 Andersen Capital Management创始人Peter Andersen称，这一决定是“董事会治理不善的教科书式案例”，并质疑董事会不可能在如此短的时间内完成充分尽职调查。他认为，市场的积极反应更多是押注英伟达将继续供货、业务照常运转，而非对董事会决策程序的认可。 公司治理专家质疑：董事会为何突然转向？ 一些公司治理人士对英伟达董事会的反转提出质疑。 Soundboard Governance创始人Doug Chia表示：“我实在无法理解……这真的非常反常。董事会为什么要这么做？此前这件事明明已经尘埃落定，已经成为过去。” 科罗拉多大学博尔德分校法学教授、公司治理专家Ann Lipton认为，董事会很可能担心自身是否履行了监督责任，以及由此产生的法律责任。 她指出，特朗普政府的介入为董事会提供了某种法律层面的保障：“特朗普政府昨天所做的，是向董事会保证其在法律层面有保障。” 耶鲁大学管理学院领导力教授Jeffrey Sonnenfeld则提醒：“董事会应该创造长期价值，而不是追求短期股价飙涨。” 他还警告，此次决定可能影响员工士气，并使公司面临更严格的政治审查。 国安争议：不能让市场回报凌驾于监管之上 黄仁勋回归并未消除围绕英伟达对华业务及国家安全风险的疑虑。特朗普称，美国政府没有理由认为黄仁勋回归会带来国家安全风险，并表示司法部长已确认政府没有证据显示黄仁勋从事违法行为。但美国国会议员并未因此停止追问。 民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦称，恢复黄仁勋职务是“鲁莽的决定”，并要求特朗普政府向国会解释哪些高级官员向英伟达董事会提供了意见。 共和党参议员约翰·科宁也在社交媒体上质疑：“没有国家安全风险？依据是什么？” 媒体指出，美国国会两党议员均要求进一步调查，并推动收紧芯片出口限制。 前拜登政府白宫技术政策和国家安全官员、现任哥伦比亚大学研究人员Aaron Bartnick认为，白宫应公开更多有关黄仁勋与国外企业往来的信息，尤其是特朗普政府据此认定其复职不构成国家安全风险的依据。 他警告：“若不然，他们向其他美国企业以及美国的对手传递的信息就是：只要股价足够高，国家安全就可以被忽视。” 硅谷欢迎回归，马斯克称错误得到纠正 科技行业对黄仁勋复职的反应则明显偏向支持。 特斯拉及SpaceX CEO埃隆·马斯克在旗下社交平台发文称：“错误已经得到纠正。” OpenAI CEO萨姆·奥尔特曼则仅发文写道：“Jensen！”英伟达杰出科学家、机器人业务主管Jim Fan也发文称：“黄仁勋2.0（Jensen 2.0）！”暗示黄仁勋回归后将开启新的阶段。 第一财经报道，英伟达研究院高级研究科学家Zhiding Yu也转发了黄仁勋登台的视频，并配文欢迎其回归。 这些支持并非完全出于情感。马斯克旗下的AI业务、奥尔特曼领导的OpenAI以及众多科技企业，都高度依赖英伟达提供的AI芯片和计算基础设施。黄仁勋回归有助于稳定英伟达与整个AI产业链之间的合作预期。 英伟达股价大涨，做空基金盘中暴跌91% 市场对黄仁勋回归的反应迅速而强烈。英伟达股价盘中涨幅一度超过36%，市值增加逾9000亿美元，纳指和标普500指数也显著走高，AI相关股票随之反弹。路透社指出，英伟达领导层不确定性一度冲击全球AI交易，黄仁勋回归则重新提振了市场信心。 据报道，一只提供英伟达三倍杠杆反向敞口的欧洲上市ETF在美股开盘后暴跌约91%，随后暂停交易。该基金上周五收盘时资产规模约为300万美元。与此同时，部分此前减持英伟达的投资者也改变策略。Founder ETFs首席投资官Lauren Cassidy此前已卖出一半英伟达持仓，原计划在90天内清仓，但在黄仁勋复职后决定将股票全部买回。 不过，AI交易面临的挑战并未随黄仁勋回归而消失。 Gabelli Funds投资组合经理Hendi Susanto称：“尽管AI产业链企业持续报告强劲需求，AI交易仍需面对融资、地缘政治、行业持续性以及市场质疑等诸多噪音。” 复职并非风波终点，英伟达仍面临多重审查 英伟达本周一表示，董事会此前成立的独立董事委员会将继续调查有关外国情报人员试图影响黄仁勋的事件，黄仁勋承诺配合调查。公司还成立了专门负责国家安全与出口管制事务的董事会委员会，并启动首席合规官招聘，以加强相关监督。 与此同时，美国政府对英伟达的调查及国会质询仍在继续。黄仁勋的回归暂时缓解了市场对公司领导层和AI产业链支持力度的担忧，却没有回答董事会为何在短短数日内改变决定、特朗普政府究竟向董事会提供了哪些信息，以及英伟达能否妥善处理对华业务与国家安全审查等问题。 对英伟达而言，黄仁勋重新掌舵或许是市场期待的结果，但董事会如何证明其决策独立性、监督程序是否充分，以及公司能否在商业利益与监管要求之间划清边界，仍将是这场风波留下的长期考验。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 黄仁勋回归点燃科技债反弹，全球信用风险指标大幅回落
articles.summary: 全球信用市场周一全面上扬。随着英伟达董事会宣布恢复Jensen Huang的首席执行官职务，科技公司债券强势反弹，信用风险指标录得数月来最大单日改善，为投资者提供了一定程度的喘息空间。 衡量投资级信用风险的CDX投资级指数利差周一盘中跌幅创4月8日以来最大单日降幅。欧洲高评级与高收益债券风险指标同步走低，高收益债券对应的信用风险反向指标升幅则创下七个月来之最。 股市方面，英伟达股价最高飙升37%，创2000年以来最大单日涨幅。 此前一周，市场经历了大幅抛售，英伟达、Meta Platforms及SpaceX等主要科技公司的信用违约互换（CDS）成本急剧攀升。 周一的反弹虽有所收复失地，但上述公司的CDS利差仅部分回吐了此前涨幅，市场情绪尚未完全平复。 交易员：AI交易逻辑能否维系是关键 Allspring Global Investments高级固定收益交易员Mark Clegg表示，"大家都在四处张望，密切观察形势。"他指出， "自2025年春季关税冲击以来，我们没有见过这样的市场波动，但AI交易逻辑能够保持完整是个积极信号。" 这一表态折射出市场对Jensen Huang复职更深层的关切——英伟达不仅是一家芯片公司，更是全球AI融资生态的核心纽带。 今年早些时候，英伟达已通过发行高评级债券筹资250亿美元，AI初创企业、算力提供商及大模型开发商均高度依赖英伟达的多十亿美元级别投资与财务背书。 英伟达是信用市场流动性锚点 英伟达在美国信用衍生品市场的系统性地位不容忽视。与英伟达挂钩的衍生品是美国CDS市场成交最为活跃的品种之一，该公司亦是最新一期CDX投资级指数中流动性最强的成分名称之一。 正因如此，围绕英伟达高管层的任何风吹草动都会迅速传导至信用市场。 Jensen Huang在被解雇不足两周后即告复职，消息落地后市场情绪明显改善，但分析人士指出，CDS利差仅收复部分失地，意味着投资者对公司治理稳定性的疑虑尚未完全消散。 信用市场反弹力度仍有局限 尽管周一数据显示信用市场出现明显反弹，但整体修复程度依然有限。 科技公司CDS利差仅部分回落，表明市场在欢迎人事变动的同时，对未来不确定性保持审慎。 投资者普遍关注的核心问题在于，英伟达能否在管理层更迭风波后维持其在AI供应链与资本市场中的核心枢纽地位，以及由此衍生的AI债券融资浪潮是否会持续。 周一信用市场的修复行情为近期遭受冲击的债券投资者带来一定宽慰，但市场是否已真正翻篇，仍有待后续观察。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 不信了！大摩：我们喊"拥抱风险"，客户却在往回缩
articles.summary: 市场波动加剧之际，摩根士丹利坚持超配全球股票的策略正面临越来越多客户的质疑。该行首席经济学家Seth Carpenter在新加坡亚太峰会后表示，其倡导的“拥抱风险”策略引发了迄今最强烈的客户质疑。 Carpenter指出， 与客户交流时，一个明显的共同点是，投资者对经济预测本身并没有太大分歧，但对当前环境下继续“拥抱风险”的策略存在强烈抵触。 峰会结束当天美股继续下跌，也反映出市场谨慎情绪仍在升温。 标普500指数此前一度跌破200日均线，VIX恐慌指数逼近30，投资者积极寻求短期保护。与此同时，垃圾债利差创下2026年以来最大单周走阔纪录，黄金、白银近期也出现明显回调，风险资产整体承压。 AI资本支出是大摩看多的核心依据 摩根士丹利维持乐观立场，主要基于对AI资本支出周期的信心。Carpenter认为，美国经济增长很大程度上依赖AI相关投资和居民消费。AI繁荣推升家庭财富，进而支撑消费支出，因此AI投资周期能否持续，也关系到美国经济增长前景。 该行还将AI视为全球性增长动力： 美国资本支出带动亚洲出口，亚洲自身的资本开支周期也在逐步拓宽。这一判断是摩根士丹利超配亚太股票的重要依据。 但市场走势与这一逻辑出现背离。对冲基金持续削减亚洲AI相关敞口，韩国KOSPI指数跌破5000点，SK海力士等核心供应链股票也面临抛售压力。尽管部分标的估值有所回落，但技术面走弱和盈利增长可持续性受到质疑，仍令投资者保持谨慎。 通胀走势是最大不确定因素 相比增长前景，Carpenter对通胀走势的判断更缺乏把握。摩根士丹利预计， 通胀将在明年一季度见顶，随后逐步回落，发达市场央行的加息幅度也将低于市场当前定价。不过，他坦言，通胀高于预期的可能性明显大于低于预期。 通胀上行的驱动因素，将决定其对市场的影响。如果源于能源冲击并导致货币政策过度收紧，经济增长和风险资产都将面临压力；但如果主要由需求走强和企业定价能力提升推动，企业名义盈利增长则有望抵消部分利率上升的影响，股票也可能发挥一定的通胀对冲作用。 大摩坚持拥抱风险，但承认市场仍有波折 Carpenter强调，摩根士丹利的策略是“拥抱风险”，而不是认为最坏时刻已经过去。从现在到2027年底，市场仍可能受到多重因素扰动，包括通胀意外反弹、地缘政治风险、美国政府关门及债务上限争议，以及欧洲选举和法国财政问题。 该行资产策略师已针对各类资产列出多空情景，经济学家也同步评估了增长前景的上下行风险。不过， 摩根士丹利目前仍认为，绝大多数证据指向经济增长保持稳健，即使通胀维持黏性，也不足以从根本上改变这一趋势。 市场方面，黄金周线RSI已降至2022年以来最超卖水平，白银周线RSI也从90上方降至30，贵金属市场波动明显加剧。野村证券则认为，如果市场波动率回落、股市企稳，交易商和CTA策略可能带来被动买盘，为市场提供支撑，但前提是股市能够在7200点附近企稳。 眼下，摩根士丹利仍坚持超配全球股票，而客户更倾向于降低风险敞口。双方的分歧，最终将取决于AI投资能否持续支撑经济增长，以及通胀是否按预期回落。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 报道：三星未来三年存储产能接近售罄，客户抢长约至2031年
articles.summary: AI基础设施建设浪潮持续重塑全球内存半导体格局。 据韩国《经济论坛》援引行业消息人士报道， 三星电子2027年至2029年间的内存制造产能大部分已通过合同锁定，部分客户甚至寻求将长期供应协议延伸至2031年。这意味着全球最大内存制造商的产能或将被提前预定长达五年。 这一局面折射出当前市场的供需严峻程度。 行业消息人士估计，领先内存制造商目前仅能满足客户约60%至70%的需求，而供应紧张态势可能在2027年进一步加剧。 三星此前已确认，其2027年高带宽内存（HBM）供应已全部售罄，行业消息人士进一步指出，2027年传统DRAM晶圆产能同样已基本耗尽。 对投资者而言，上述动态表明AI驱动的内存需求短期内难以消退，三星等内存厂商的营收能见度有望显著提升，但不同细分市场的前景分化——NAND市场的中长期走势面临更多不确定性。 报道发布前，三星周一收跌3.06%。 长期供应协议加速落地，三星锁定中长期产能六至七成 三星在2026年第三季度财报发布会上正式确认，已与10家主要客户签署长期供应协议（LTA），另有10家客户的谈判正在推进，部分已接近尾声。 根据《经济论坛》的最新报道， 三星计划在2030年前将中长期内存产能的约60%至70%纳入多年期合同框架，以在为大型科技客户保障供应的同时，增强自身营收的稳定性与可预测性。 部分客户目前据报正寻求将协议延伸至2031年，相关安排可能涉及预付款机制及合同定价条款，旨在为双方提供应对未来市场波动的保护。 这些长期锁定安排在当前供应紧张的背景下尤为值得关注——现有客户不仅在寻求延长协议，还在已有承诺之外继续争取额外产能分配，凸显出可用产能竞争的激烈程度。 HBM生产挤压传统DRAM，扩产效果短期受限 供应紧张并非仅集中于HBM领域。随着制造商优先保障面向AI加速器和数据中心的高利润产品，传统DRAM供应据报亦日趋紧张。 这背后有一个结构性制约因素：生产先进HBM需消耗大量DRAM晶圆资源，导致制造商即便加大投资，也难以迅速扩大传统内存的实际产出。 三星自身也警告称，额外资本支出不会立即转化为更高的内存产量，新制造设施需要数年时间才能正式投产。 这一现象对消费级市场同样构成影响。最新进展表明，若AI基础设施投资维持当前节奏，DRAM供应的实质性缓解或将遥遥无期。 NAND市场前景存在分歧，不同细分市场走势或现分化 与DRAM的持续供应紧张形成对比，NAND市场的中长期前景存在明显不确定性。 研究机构集邦咨询（TrendForce）近期预测，NAND合同价格可能于2027年第一季度开始下滑，面临需求减少和供给增加的风险。 据韩国媒体报道，企业级NAND及SSD需求目前仍然强劲，部分供应商难以满足特定客户需求，但这并不改变该市场中长期供需趋势正在转向的判断。 这一分化表明，DRAM、HBM与NAND三个细分市场的需求状况可能存在相当大的差异，投资者在评估内存行业前景时需区别对待不同产品线的供需动态。 值得注意的是，长期供应协议本身并不必然保证内存价格持续高企，需求条件的转变最终可能缓解部分市场压力。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 吴悦风旗下私募陷清盘传闻，最新回应：是假的，不会清盘；基金主要投向韩国存储股票，并且买了一些杠杆ETF，因此放大了波动
articles.summary: 11月23日，一则传言在社交媒体发酵，有消息称，知名私募投资人吴悦风管理的基金已清盘。截图显示，吴悦风的账号“月风投资笔记”在与“苏姿丰”的对话中表示“结束了，一场游戏一场梦”。 据中证金牛座报道，对于基金清盘的消息，吴悦风回应记者称： “不用管，是假的。（市场）已经到底了，不会做清盘这种事情。” 吴悦风表示， 基金主要投向韩国存储股票，并且买了一些杠杆ETF，因此放大了波动。 尤其是在9月份下跌时，采取了越跌越加的操作，事后看加仓时间过早了。 据私募排排网数据，截至11月13日，吴悦风管理的嘉越月风投资创世号净值为0.3697元，近一年跌幅39.92%，成立四年以来最大回撤超过84%。 作为社交媒体上拥有数百万粉丝的财经大V，吴悦风此前经常通过账号“月风投资笔记”发表观点。此前，其先后在安邦保险资管公司任职权益投资经理与股指期货专业风险责任人，在沣京资本任职合伙人、基金经理，其一举一动备受市场关注。离开沣京资本后，吴悦风担任嘉越投资合伙人、基金经理，他管理的这只产品嘉越月风投资创世号因净值多次大起大落引发市场关注。 今年，这只基金一度暴涨，从“三毛基”涨回“两元基”，今年四月、五月、六月单月收益分别高达98.65%、69.67%、12.76%。 本文来源： 每日经济新闻 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 美国商业活动扩张势头在11月明显降温，高物价、运输延误与供应瓶颈共同拖累制造业与服务业表现，尽管整体仍处于扩张区间。 周一，标普全球数据显示， 11月美国综合采购经理人指数（PMI）初值较上月下降1.3个百分点至54.6，为近四个月低位。制造业分项指数滑落至54.5，创三个月新低；服务业活动指数同样回落至四个月低位。 11月供应链压力明显恶化。 据标普全球援引全球贸易扰动与运输延误因素，制造商供应商交货时间延长幅度为2022年以来最大。反映需求状况的新订单分项指数扩张步伐亦降至7月以来最慢水平，显示终端需求动能有所减弱。 从需求侧看，强劲的消费者支出、人工智能相关投资以及国防开支，为美国企业提供了有力支撑并推动今年盈利增长。展望后市，标普全球表示，11月中期选举结束后企业信心出现反弹，但政治不确定性犹存叠加通胀高企，仍对增长预期形成制约。 价格指数上涨速度为8月以来最慢，就业指数连续第五个月维持扩张 在通胀层面，价格分项指数虽以8月以来最慢速度上涨，但企业面临的投入成本上升与薪资压力仍处高位， 这对正致力于压制通胀的美联储构成潜在挑战。 标普全球市场情报首席商业经济学家Chris Williamson表示，"生活成本高企及由此引发的购买力承压，是当前核心隐忧，调查中的价格指标所处水平意味着，未来数月通胀仍将大幅高于美联储2%的目标。" 尽管整体活动降温，就业市场表现仍具韧性。 综合就业分项指数连续第五个月维持在扩张区间。 Chris Williamson指出，制造业与服务业活动依然"强劲亮眼"，两大部门均在持续增加用工，"就业人数增长态势表明，11月非农就业数据有望再度录得强劲表现"。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 特朗普火速力挺黄仁勋复职：正确且恰当决定，美政府无证据表明他有违法行为
articles.summary: 英伟达宣布董事会决定恢复黄仁勋总裁、首席执行官（CEO）及董事职务后不到10分钟，美国总统特朗普便公开力挺这一决定，称美国政府没有理由认为黄仁勋回归会对国家安全构成风险。 据新华社，特朗普23日在社交媒体发文说，英伟达董事会让黄仁勋重新担任CEO一职是“正确且恰当的决定”。他表示，美国政府没有理由认为黄仁勋回归英伟达会对国家安全构成任何风险。美国司法部长已确认，美国政府没有证据表明其有任何不合法行为。 特朗普发帖表示，美国需要黄仁勋继续领导英伟达，以确保公司乃至美国经济的成功与繁荣。他称，自己已经与黄仁勋相识，认为他是一位“伟大的爱国者和国家瑰宝”。 不过，特朗普同时要求英伟达继续彻底调查公司是否遵守美国出口管制规定，确保履行法律义务以及保护美国国家安全的“爱国责任”。 特朗普周一几度直接喊话英伟达董事会 在英伟达董事会宣布复职决定前，23日周一稍早，特朗普就已在社交媒体发文，直接敦促英伟达董事会重新聘用黄仁勋。 他当时表示，希望英伟达董事会重新聘用黄仁勋，认为这将是对公司和美国最有利的选择。 特朗普此次表态意味着，他不仅在董事会作出决定前公开支持黄仁勋回归，也在复职消息公布后第一时间为这一决定背书。 特朗普发帖后，据媒体报道，他周一还表示，强烈认为黄仁勋应该复出。他说，我们必须保护我们的天才，失去黄仁勋的智慧才是最大的威胁。黄仁勋生产了不起的芯片。 特朗普称，美国已经对黄仁勋进行了“非常彻底的调查”。他曾直接与英伟达董事会对话，发现董事会是理性的。特朗普称，他不了解英伟达董事会的成员，但他们做的不错。 董事会一致通过复职，调查仍将继续 英伟达23日宣布，董事会一致通过恢复黄仁勋总裁、CEO及董事职务，即刻生效。董事会表示，经过与黄仁勋多轮讨论和会面，对其坦诚程度及领导公司能力感到满意。董事会还透露，在作出决定前征询了美国政府高层意见，并据此认定黄仁勋复职不会构成国家安全风险。 值得注意的是，在力挺黄仁勋回归的同时，特朗普并未要求英伟达停止内部调查。 英伟达董事会23日也表示，针对黄仁勋此前疑似成为外国情报行动目标一事，独立董事组成的调查委员会仍将继续调查，黄仁勋承诺配合。此外，公司已成立专门的国家安全与出口管制委员会，并计划新设首席合规官职位，加强贸易合规及国家安全风险管理。 黄仁勋此前于11月12日辞去英伟达CEO及董事职务。此次复职意味着董事会扭转了此前的立场。 英伟达董事会主席哈维·琼斯曾在上周二美股盘后的公司业绩电话会上表示，公司无意恢复黄仁勋的CEO职务，而此次董事会最终一致同意其回归。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 八个月配额后，刚果金出口全面暂停，钴市再迎政策变数
articles.summary: 全球最大钴生产国刚果民主共和国宣布，将于本月底起再次暂停钴出口，以遏制国际钴价持续下跌，并缓解全球市场供应过剩压力。 11月23日，据彭博报道，刚果政府监管机构ARECOMS周一发表声明称， 自11月30日起暂停所有钴出口，暂停期限暂未确定。 ARECOMS表示，此举旨在“解决国际市场供应过剩问题，推动市场可持续再平衡”。这是刚果自2025年2月首次实施全面出口禁令以来，第二次采取类似措施。 此次禁令出台之际，钴价正面临较大下行压力。刚果主要出口产品钴氢氧化物的价格自今年4月触及峰值后几近腰斩，全球需求疲软及再生钴供应增加进一步加剧了市场供需失衡。新一轮出口管控将影响全球钴供应，也可能改变矿企和下游买家的库存及采购安排。 价格持续下跌，配额制度未能稳住市场 刚果于2025年2月首次实施全面钴出口禁令，八个月后以严格配额制度取而代之，但未能阻止钴价持续回落。根据Fastmarkets数据，钴氢氧化物价格在首次禁令实施后一度上涨逾四倍，随后从4月高点大幅回落，几乎抹去此前涨幅。 ARECOMS在声明中表示，此次决定是综合考虑钴价自6月以来显著且持续下跌后作出的。当前市场面临全球钴消费放缓、库存增加及投机活动等多重压力。该机构已于11月9日召开会议，批准此次临时出口暂停决定。 新一轮禁令也将波及主要钴生产商。目前持有最大出口配额的企业包括洛阳钼业、嘉能可及欧亚资源集团。现行配额制度已将刚果钴出口量限制在2024年全国产量的一半以下。 刚果政府数据显示， 今年前九个月，该国矿企共出口钴61441吨，远低于2024年同期的逾145,000吨 。此次再次暂停出口，意味着全球钴原料供应将进一步受到限制。 需求疲软，印尼或填补部分供应缺口 钴主要用于电动汽车及消费电子产品的可充电电池。分析师指出，消费电子领域需求尤其疲软，是近期钴价承压的重要原因之一。 供应端方面，刚果此前约占全球矿产钴供应量的四分之三。 作为全球第二大钴生产国，印度尼西亚或将从新一轮禁令中受益。该国依托本土镍矿资源，在冶炼过程中生产含钴中间产品，有望填补刚果出口暂停留下的部分供应缺口。 ARECOMS表示，计划在四个月后重新评估禁令，届时将综合考量钴市场走势、库存水平及全球供需平衡状况。同时，该机构还将利用出口暂停期审查并调整配额分配机制。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
